doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Race among musicians and Duke Ellington's kindness
summary: Iola says musicians care whether you can play; Duke told Dave to go to New York and offered the Hickory House.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Do you think there’s any political correctness that still goes on in the business between black musicians and white musicians?

I think there was a time when that was an issue for some people. I see less and less of it. And you know among the people who were really firmly established, Duke for example, he never saw any of that. And I think for most musicians, can you play? And are you a decent person to get along with? And that’s about all they ask. And Duke was very good

to Dave. And before Dave was known, Duke came into a club in San Francisco and talked to him, and said, “You know you should go to New York. If you’re really going to make it you have to go to New York. And I can get you into the Hickory House.” So that showed, in Duke’s mind, I’m sure that didn’t enter into it.
